title: 028 · Why? #16: the six trig ratios are six real lines (the studied reel's look, voiced af_heart; cot and cosec drawn correctly)

captions.instagram:
NDA Maths · Trigonometry. sin, cos, tan, sec, cot, cosec aren't just ratios. On a circle of radius 1, each one is a real line 👇

sin θ is the height, cos θ is the base.
Tangent: draw the line that touches the circle at (1, 0) and stretch the radius to meet it. That piece is tan θ, on the touching line. That's the name: tangent = touching.
The slant from the centre to it cuts through the circle: sec θ (secant = to cut). Pythagoras: 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ.
Do the same with the line touching the top: cot θ and cosec θ, and 1 + cot²θ = cosec²θ.

NDA asked about this in 2024 (II), Q79: lim θ→π/2 (sec θ − tan θ) = ? sec θ − tan θ = (1 − sin θ)/cos θ = cos θ/(1 + sin θ) → 0, so (B) 0. In the picture: as θ grows, both lines shoot up but their gap shrinks.
